cohort: Women retrospectively screened and stratified into three groups based on CPD-related dystocia and delivery method: planned cesarean deliveries for prenatal high CPD risk, emergency cesarean deliveries due to CPD-related dystocia, and vaginal deliveries without CPD occurrence.
finding: A random forest machine learning model, utilizing routine clinical parameters, effectively identified high-risk cephalopelvic disproportion (CPD)-related dystocia prenatally with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.824, outperforming traditional clinical judgment.
mod_finding: The study highlighted that obstetricians' prenatal assessments based on clinical experience often fail to identify all CPD-related dystocia cases, leading to emergency cesarean deliveries (comprising 26.25% of all emergency CDs performed during labor) among patients initially deemed low-risk.
